title: 5-Repo Diverse Corpus — Build Infrastructure Blocker

dependencyPrep.notes: All 5 repos were successfully shallow-cloned. Build of DollarLint itself failed before validation could begin. No validation output was produced. Previous runs all occurred on macOS with a populated module cache; this is the first run on a GitHub Actions Linux runner. The MCP server appears unable to exec the Go compiler.
dependencyPrep.error: exitCode 1, duration 0s — immediate failure, likely missing GOMODCACHE or GOROOT not accessible to the MCP server subprocess in the Linux CI environment

findings: BLOCKER: go build failed with exitCode 1, duration 0s — immediate failure in the Linux CI environment. DollarLint binary could not be produced, so no validation was run against any of the 5 corpus repos (gitea, prettier, fastapi, neovim, pnpm).
All 5 repo clones succeeded: gitea, prettier, fastapi, neovim, pnpm.
Previous weekly runs all succeeded on macOS (developer machine) with a pre-populated Go module cache. This is the first run on a GitHub Actions Linux runner where no GOMODCACHE exists.
The MCP server (dollarlint-repo) running as an HTTP service at 127.0.0.1:8080 appears to not inherit the GOROOT/PATH environment set by the workflow runner, causing the go binary to fail immediately.
Proxy.golang.org and sum.golang.org are in the allowed-domains list, so module downloads would succeed if the Go compiler could be invoked.

Recommendation: pre-build the DollarLint binary as part of the workflow setup steps before the agent session, or ensure GOROOT and GOMODCACHE are accessible to the MCP server's subprocess environment.

productRecommendations.recommendation: Pre-build the dollarlint binary (e.g., via a workflow `go build` step before the agent runs) so that the MCP server's real_world_run_corpus tool can use the pre-built artifact with build:false.
productRecommendations.rationale: The MCP server subprocess cannot reliably execute go build in the Linux CI environment. Building the binary in a dedicated pre-step sidesteps this entirely and is more reliable across environments.

productRecommendations.recommendation: Add a GOMODCACHE setup step or cache the Go module cache in the workflow so that go build can succeed in CI without downloading modules each run.
productRecommendations.rationale: Even if the GOROOT issue is fixed, a cold module cache means downloading all dependencies on every run, which is slow and fragile.

productRecommendations.recommendation: Document that real_world_run_corpus build:true requires the MCP server to have access to go in PATH with GOROOT and GOMODCACHE configured; add an explicit error message when go cannot be found.
productRecommendations.rationale: The current 0-second exitCode:1 failure gives no diagnostic output, making it hard to understand what went wrong.

followUp: Fix the CI setup so go build works: either pre-build in a workflow step, or ensure the MCP server inherits the correct Go environment (GOROOT, GOPATH, PATH)
Retry this same corpus (gitea, prettier, fastapi, neovim, pnpm) once the build infrastructure is resolved
Consider adding a smoke-test step that verifies bin/dollarlint --version before the agent session begins
